theory.text: Determine whether each statement agrees with factual information in the passage. TRUE: supported. FALSE: contradicted. NOT GIVEN: insufficient information. A missing fact is not automatically false.
Key skills: Keywords, paraphrases, negatives and limiting words such as all, only and some.

guide.text: Underline the claim  locate related information  compare the complete meaning  decide TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.

small.text: Text: “The museum opened in 2004 and began offering free entry in 2010.”
E1. The museum started operating in 2004.E2. Admission was free from the first day.E3. The museum is the city’s most visited attraction.

full.text: A university established its botanical garden in 1998. In its first year, the garden held 120 plant species. A new greenhouse was constructed in 2012, allowing staff to cultivate tropical plants. The garden welcomes school groups throughout the year, but the report gives no visitor breakdown.
Write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.1. The garden was established in 1998.2. A greenhouse had already been built before 2000.3. Most visitors are university students.

rows: Free entry began in 2010, not on opening day in 2004.
No visitor popularity ranking is provided.
The greenhouse was built in 2012, not before 2000.
Choosing FALSE when evidence is missing
Use FALSE only if the passage contradicts the statement; otherwise consider NOT GIVEN.
Choosing a heading because one word matches
Summarise the paragraph’s full main idea.
Answer using the evidence in the passage only.
Recheck NO MORE THAN ... WORDS instructions and spelling.
Check the complete sentence against evidence.
Spending too long on one question
Move on and return after easier questions.
Confusing a quoted opinion with the writer’s stance
Identify who holds the opinion before answering YES / NO / NOT GIVEN.
